scientific_question: Do permitted experimental records and Anarres measurements improve candidate-environment selection on complete held-out studies?
independent_unit: candidate training intervention; seeds are aggregated before prediction and scoring
history_rule: Cross-history conditions contain only candidate outcomes from studies other than the held-out study. Target outcomes and all target-study outcomes remain absent.
panel_rule: One query ranks every candidate in one matched target panel. Candidate order is deterministic and outcome-blind.
target: panel-normalized utility in [0,1], used for ordering rather than cross-domain absolute calibration

model.retry_rule: Repeat the identical request once only when the server returns no valid final JSON. Record both attempts and charge all tokens.
model.output_constraint: strict JSON schema with exact candidate keys
model.selection_reason: The checkpoint is Apache-2.0, fits on one available B200, predates the released Anarres outcomes, and is the strongest already-cached open reasoning model qualified for this comparison.

advancement_rule: A later prospective test requires improvement over the strongest eligible native or matched-history baseline after inference and measurement cost, plus an explicit abstention rule. This retrospective comparison runs regardless of the earlier structured baseline result.
claim_boundary: Retrospective record-conditioned replay. Public-record contamination, small independent-study count, and heterogeneous targets limit generalization.
